'beginning': two, human legs. Hence two and a pair of human legs come to mean beginning.
'stubborn': headed, beginning, heads. Picture these two with their giant, swelled heads, each vying for the favors of heaven, a stubborn grimace on their faces.
'mediocre': drop, wind. While we refer to something insignificant as a “drop in the bucket,” the kanji for mediocre suggests the image of a “drop in the wind.”

'defeat': bound up, shellfish, oysters, shell. Now imagine two oysters engaged in shell-toshell combat, the one who is defeated being bound and gagged with seaweed, the victor towering triumphantly over it.
'ten thousand': bind up, one, bound up. Japanese counts higher numbers in units of ten thousand, unlike the West, which advances according to units of one thousand.
'phrase': bound up, mouth. After all, a phrase is nothing more than a number of words bound up tightly and neatly so that they will fit in your mouth.
'texture': wind, part of the body. So whenever a part of the body gets exposed to the wind, its texture is affected.
'decameron': days, bound together. Actually, it refers to a journey of ten days taken by a band of people—that is, a group of people bound together for the days of the decameron.

'fish guts'. Among its many other meanings are “pure,” “tasteful,” “quaint,” and—get this!—fish guts.
'riot': tongue, fishhook, hook. This kanji shows what happens to a rioting tongue: it gets “barbed” like a fishhook, and sets to attacking the opposition, to hook them as it were.
'straightaway': needle, eye, eye of a needle, fishhook. Together they represent the eye of a needle.
'true': eye of the needle, tool. Here again we meet the composite element, eye of the needle, which here combines with tool to give us a measure of what is true and what is not.
'left': by one's side, craft, side, crafts. Conveniently, the left has traditionally been considered the “sinister” side, where dark and occult crafts are cultivated.
'right': mouth, side. Imagine a little mouth hanging down by your side—like a little voice of conscience—telling you the right thing to do.

'tribute': money, craft. Little wonder that this ancient craft of getting money by calling it a tribute has given way to a name closer to how it feels to those who pay it: a tax.
'paragraph': head, craft, heading, heads. When we think of a paragraph, we immediately think of a heading device to break a text into parts.
'sword'. Although this character no longer looks very much like a sword, it does have some resemblance to the handle of the sword.
'blade': dagger, drop of. Think of using a dagger as a razor blade, and it shouldn't be hard to imagine cutting yourself.
'cut': dagger, seven, diced, dicing. It is hard to think of cutting anything with a knife without imagining one of those skillful Japanese chefs.
'shining': seduce, sun. Let the key word suggest shining one's shoes, the purpose of which is to seduce the sun down on them for all to see.

'sand': few, stones. Good sand for beaches has few or no stones in it.
'plane': sabers, sparks. Indeed, you can almost see the sparks fly from their sabers.
'ray': little, human legs. There are really only 2 primitives here, little and human legs.

'exquisite': woman, few. When we refer to a woman as exquisite, we mean to praise her as the sort of person we meet but few and far between.
'focus': eye, few. When we think of focusing on something, we usually take it in a metaphorical sense, though the literal sense is not far behind.

'strange': st bernard dog, can, mouth, nails. Now all we need do is create a fictitious “Strange But True” column in the Sunday funnies, featuring a St.
'stream'. We have taken the image of a river stream over into English to describe things that fall down in straight lines, or ripple along in lines.
'state': drops of, stream. Here we see drops of land (little islets) rising up out of a stream, creating a kind of sandbar or breakwater.
'obey': stream, head. Either one obeys the person who is head of an organization or else obeys by following the stream of opinion (“current” practice, we call it).
'water': walking stick, droplets. Should you have any difficulty remembering it, simply think of a walking stick being dropped vertically into the water, sending droplets out in all four directions.
'icicle': water, drop, walking stick. The extra drop to the left, added as a second stroke, changes the picture from a splash caused by a walking stick dropped into water to form an icicle.
'eternity': water, drop of water. Well, reading this character from top to bottom, we see “eternity in a drop of water.”

'spring': water, white. Call to mind the image of a fresh, bubbling spring of water, and you will probably notice how the top of the spring you are thinking of, the part where the “bubbling” goes on, is all white.

'meadow': springs, cliff. Now if you can see Schwester Maria skipping along merrily, dodging in and out of the springs, and then falling headlong over the cliff, you have a ridiculous story that should help fix this kanji in memory.
'petition': meadow, head. Then just picture people kneeling hopefully before it, petitioning for whatever it is they want.
'swim': water, eternity, eternal. Knowing how much children like swimming, what could be a better image of eternal bliss than an endless expanse of water to swim in without a care in the world?
'marsh': water, seduce, seductions. Why certain land becomes marshy is probably due to the fact that it felt thirsty, and so tried its best to seduce the water over to its side.
'open sea': in the middle of, water. The key word open sea readily suggests being out in the middle of a great body of water.
'creek': water, craft. Unlike the river, the ocean, the lake, and the pond, the creek is often no more then a dribble of water trickling down a small gully.
'soup': water, ten. To make soup, one begins with water and then starts adding things to it, often leftovers from the icebox.
'tide': water, morning, eventide. Here we have the morning-tide, its complement.
'source': water, meadow. Both in its etymology (it has a common parent with the word “surge”) and in popular usage, source suggests the place water comes from.
'lively': tongues, water. When we speak of a lively personality or a lively party, we immediately think of a lot of chatter.

'extinguish': water, drops of water, drop of water, spark. In the best of all possible worlds, the most efficient way to extinguish a fire would be to see that each drop of water hits one spark of the conflagration.
'but of course': teenager, water. So water and teenager combine to give us but of course.

'lake': water, old, flesh, waters. Well, here is a legend about people being set adrift in the waters of a stormy lake because their flesh had gotten too old to bear the burdens of life.
'fathom': water, rule, rule water, ruler. Be sure to picture yourself fathoming a body of water several hundred feet deep by using a ruler of gargantuan proportions.
'spit': mouth, dirt. It is not hard to imagine what you might do if you got a mouth full of dirt.
'pressure': soil, cliff. One of the things that causes the erosion of soil is the excessive pressure of the topsoil on the lower soil.
'cape': land, soil, strange, odd. The soil on the left tells us we have to do with land, and the strange on the right tells us it is a cape where unusual things go on.

'seal': glue, ivy. Instead of using the traditional wax seal, you glue a sprig of ivy on the outside.

'level': soil, ladle, drops of soil, drop. The excess drops of soil are brushed off the top, which accounts for the added drop at the ladle's edge.

'inflammation': fire, hearth. A fire belongs in the hearth, not over it.
'anxiety': head, afire. The head is set afire, causing deep torment of spirit (and a whopper of a headache).

'disaster': floods, fires, flood, fire. Of all of nature's disasters, this kanji picks out two of the worst: floods and fires.
'ashes': fire, fireplace, cliff. Now what do you do with that bucket of ashes you have just cleaned out of the fireplace?
'spot': fire, fortune, telling, cauldron. Although nobody ever thought of such a thing before—as least as far as I know, they didn't—imagine using those spots as a technique for fortune-telling.
'illuminate': shine, oven, fire, shining. If you glaze a pot and put it into the oven to fire it, you in fact illuminate it.

'black ink': dirt, black. Here it is used to mark off the dirt with black lines for a football game (played, I presume, on a white field).

'same': one, mouth, hood, cowl. Here we see the monk's cowl, drawn down over the eyes so that all you can see when you look at him is a mouth.
'den': same, water. Now if we keep to the image of the monastic life as an image for same, we can picture a den of wild beasts dressed up in habits and living the common life in a mountain cavern.
'trunk': part of the body, same, body. The word trunk refers to the part of the body that is left when you have “truncated” all the limbs.

'esteem': little, glass canopies, littleness, mouth. The littleness is important, because what is in fact on display is the shrunken, stuffed, and mounted mouth of an esteemed ancestor.
'character': child, house. It shows us simply a child in a house.
'guard': glue, house. The whole idea of hiring guards is that they should stick like glue to your house to protect it from unwanted prowlers.
'perfect': per, factum, house, beginnings. We see a house that has been made perfectly from its beginnings in the foundation to the roof on the top.

'wee hours': house, candle. It does this by picturing a house with a candle in it.

'world': jammed, rice fields. Imagine yourself taking an air flight over a world so densely populated that every bit of it is sectioned off like a gigantic checkerboard (the rice fields).

'tea': flowers, flowering, wooden poles, umbrella. With the image of a terrace of flowering tea bushes in mind, picture very l-o-n-g wooden poles ( frame 195) placed here and there in their midst, with a tiny umbrella at the top
'fit': meeting, mouths. We know what happens when there is no meeting of minds and when people's ideas don't fit, but try to imagine what would happen to a poor couple whose mouths didn't fit.
'pagoda': dirt, flowers, fit, fitted. The two sides combine to create a great pagoda made of dirt, with flowers by the tens of thousands fitted together for the roofing of each of the layers.
'king': i beam. See what you can do to come up with a pictograph of a king's scepter here that suits your own idea of what it should look like.
'jewel': drop, scepter. Note the drop here in the king's scepter, which is exactly what you would expect it to be: a precious jewel handed down from of old as a symbol of his wealth and power.
'treasure': house, jewels. While the things we treasure most are usually of sentimental value, we take the original sense of the term treasure here and make it refer to jewels kept in one's house.

'pearl': jewel, vermilion, ball. Think of the most enormous pearl you have ever seen, a great vermilion-colored ball sitting on your ring—and making it extremely difficult to move without falling over from the weight of the thing.
'present': ball. The kanji gives us a ball in which we see the present—obviously a crystal ball that enables us to see things going on at the present in faraway places.
'lunatic': king, pack of wild dogs. Imagine one of these lycanthropes going looney and setting himself up as king of a pack of wild dogs that roams about and terrorizes innocent suburban communities.
'emperor': king, white bird, white birds. An emperor, as we all know, is a ruler—something like a king but higher in status.
'display': king, mouth. If we think of display in terms of that famous line, and the king with his head thrown back and his mouth wide open as 4 and 20 blackbirds fly in one after the other, we shall
'whole': king, umbrella. The kanji-image for wholeness depicts being “king under your own umbrella,” that is, giving order to your own life.
'plug': tree, umbrella, ball, balls. Imagine a tree with a faucet in the side out of which tennis balls are flowing, bouncing all over the ground by the hundreds.
'logic': jewel, computer, jewels. The image of logic we are given is something like a central jewel in a computer, like the jewels in old clocks that keep them running smoothly.
'lord': drop, king. Fundamentally, it means only that every person is a bit (or drop) of a king in one's own environment.
'pour': water, candlestick. Picture pouring water from a lighted candlestick.
'pillar': wooden, candlestick. The pillar referred to here is the wooden beam that stands at the entrance to a traditional Japanese house.
'gold': umbrella, scepters, drop. Anyway, we want to depict bars of gold bullion with an umbrella overhead to shade them from the heat (and perhaps to hide them as well).

'bowl': golden, books. Let bowl suggest a large and heavy golden bowl into which you are throwing all the books you own to mash them into pulp, for some outrageous reason you will have to think up yourself.
'copper': monks, metal. Picture an order of monks serving as chaplains for the police force.
'angling': fishing, golden ladle, gold. The odd thing is that your angling rod is a golden ladle which you are using to scoop goldfish out of a river.
'needle': metal, gold, needles. Since we already expect that needles are made of metal, let us picture a set of solid gold darning needles to complete the kanji.

'inscription': name, gold. Take inscription in the sense of the name you ask the jeweler to carve on a gold bracelet or inside a gold ring to identify its owner or communicate some sentimental message.
'tranquillize': metal, truth. The first lie-detector machines of the twentieth century worked by wiring pieces of metal to the body to measure the amount of sweat produced when questions were asked.
'road-way': neck, road. Think of a crowded road-way where traffic has come to a standstill—what we commonly refer to as a “bottleneck.”
'guidance': glued, road, way. When we accept someone's guidance, we permit ourselves to be glued to a certain road or way of doing something, and try to “stick” to it.

'swift': crossing, fishhook. Here we see a crossing in the form of a barbed fishhook, suggesting a swifter alternate not only to the old roundabouts but also to the “cloverleaf” design used on superhighways.
'create': way, revelation. Then recall how the way of revelation laid out in the Bible begins with the story of how God created the world out of a dark and chaotic nothingness.
'urge': way, white. To urge someone to do something, you make the way as appealing as possible, perhaps even whitewashing it a bit.
'escape': turtle, road. When escaping from something or someone, one always feels as if one is not going fast enough, like a turtle on an expressway.
'environs': daggers, road. To keep the environs clean and safe, you could cement daggers in the road, blades pointed upwards, so that no polluting traffic could pass by.
'patrol': deluge, road. A virtual deluge of motorcycle police washing down a road is this kanji's image for a patrol.
'take along': car, road, take, along. The image of the car on the road should ground your image for picking up your friends to take them along to wherever you are going.
'rut': car, baseball team. Begin with the car whose tires get caught in a rut and spin without going anywhere.
'transport': vehicle, meeting, flesh, saber. On the left we see a vehicle used for transport.
'in front': butcher, horns, before. Picture the butcher hacking away with his knife at a slab of meat on his table with a pair of ram's horns placed in front of him (or on his head, if you prefer).
'each': mouth, walking legs. In any event, here we see someone walking with his/her mouth between his/her walking legs, giving us an image of “To each his/her own.”

'status': trees, each, tree. If you can imagine trees as status symbols (as they might well be for those living in Japan's congested modern cities), then each might be aiming to have his/her own tree, just to keep up with
'abbreviation': each field. Each field has its own abbreviations (chemistry, philosophy, sports, etc.).
'guest': each house. When you are a guest in a courteous town, each household has its own way of welcoming you, and each house becomes your home.
'forehead': guest. Here, however, you are told to look above the eyes to the forehead of your guest.
'summer': head, walking legs, page. In the summer, fatigued by the heat, your head hangs down nearly as far as your walking legs, or rather, your “dragging legs.”

'dispose': walking legs, wind. Both the stretching out of the walking legs and the little bit of wind tucked in on the right suggest using one's legs to kick something out of the way, or dispose of it.
'twig': walking legs, tree. Geppetto made walking legs for his little Pinocchio from two twigs of a tree, giving him a set of “twiggy” shanks.
'fall': water, flower, each. When water falls, it splats and splashes; when flower petals fall, they float gently in the breeze.
'superfluous': weather vane, crown. Picture a weather vane beneath a regal crown, spinning round and round.
'army': crowned vehicle, chariot. The crowned vehicle depicted here is a “chariot,” symbol of an army.
'radiance': ray, chariot, rays. Now add the glittering chariot that is emitting those rays and you have radiance.
'carry': chariots, roads. A long string of “sweet” chariots “swinging low” to our roads is a sure sign that the Lord is “comin' for to carry” someone home.
'crown': glued, beginnings. By having the crown pass from one age to the next, a people keeps itself glued to its beginnings.
'dream': crown, evening, flower, eyes. To have a dream after going to bed is really the crown to a perfect evening.
'pit': whirlwind, soil. A whirlwind begins to dig its way into the soil like a drill until it makes a deep pit.

'tall': mouth, hood, top hat. Recalling an image from frame 183, first see the mouth under the extraterrestrial's glass hood, and then the mouth under the top hat of one of his mates who has tried on the strange earthling's
'receive': tall children, tall child. Tall children grow up to make better wide receivers.
'cram school': tall children, fat. The exception are the tall children who are out on the school grounds practicing sports, and the fat ones who are out there burning off calories.

'mellow': tall, fat children, oven flame. The tall and fat children from the last frame are here cast into a cauldron over an oven flame until they have sufficiently mellowed that they can return to the normal life of a

'pavilion': tall crowned nail, crown. Think of all the pavilions at some World Expo you attended or followed in the media, and you will no doubt see rising up among them the towering tall crowned nail (the crown being a
'capital': tall, little. Think of some tall, domed capital building with swarms of little folk gathered around its base, probably demonstrating for their government's attention.
'refreshing': water, capital. Since few things are as refreshing on a warm day as a cool shower (the water), here we picture a capital building treating itself to one, and in full view of everyone.
'scenery': sun, capital. Scenery is depicted as a sun rising over a capital, which is as close as some city dwellers get to natural scenery for years at a time!
'whale': fish, capital. The whale swallows a whole school of fish, who turn their new abode into a proper little fish-capital.
'cottage': lidded crock, umbrella. A lidded crock with an umbrella overhead gives us a mixture of the modern and the nostalgic in this design for a cottage.

'circumference': lidded crock, motorcycle helmet, helmet. This is so you can use it to calculate the circumference of your motorcycle helmet: just begin at a fixed point and turn the lidded crock around and around, keeping it flush against the
'week': road, lap. Picture a circular road with 7 markers on it, one for each day of the week.
'good luck': samurai, mouth. Here we see a samurai standing on a street with an open mouth, which people walk up to and look down deep inside of for good luck.
'robust': turtle, samurai. Robust is seen as a turtle turned samurai.
'villa': flowers, turtle, samurai. The villa pictured here is filled with exotic flowers at every turn, and has a pair of turtle-samurai standing before its gates.
'sell': samurai, crowns, human legs. A samurai, out of a job, is going door-to-door selling little windup crowns with human legs that run around on the floor looking like headless monarchs.
'study': child, schoolhouse, learning. The child in the little red schoolhouse is there for one reason only: to study.
'flourish': tree, schoolhouse. The botanical connotations of the word flourish (to bud and burst into bloom, much as a tree does) are part of the ideal of the schoolhouse as well.
'write': tongue wagging in his mouth, brush. The sage talks rapidly with his tongue wagging in his mouth, while the brush of the scribe runs apace to write down the master's words.

'haven': brush, water. Seeing the tiny boats of poor mortals tossed about in a stormy sea like so many corks, the All-Merciful took its brush and drew little inlets of water where the hapless creatures might seek shelter.
'breed': cow, taskmaster. Thus the taskmaster to the right forces the cow into a compromising position, so to speak, so that she and her mate can breed.

'aggression': craft, taskmasters. The special craft of successful taskmasters is their ability to remain constantly on the aggressive, never allowing their underlings a moment to ponder a counter-aggression of their own.
'failure': taskmaster, clam. The taskmaster is acknowledging the failure of a clam to make the grade in some marine school or other.
'a sheet of': taskmaster, tree. The kanji does this with a taskmaster whipping a tree into producing sheets against its will.
'happenstance': oldest taskmaster. Call it fate or providence or plain old Lady Luck, happenstance is the oldest taskmaster we know.
'awe': flowery phrases, taskmaster. Standing in awe of someone, you get self-conscious and may try to speak in flowery phrases out of veneration or fear.
'say': mouths. Of all the things we can do with our mouths, speech is the one that requires the greatest distinctness and clarity.
'admonish': awe, words. The idea of being admonished for something already sets up a superior-inferior relationship between you and the person you are supposed to stand in awe of.
'plot': words, needle. Words and a meter's needle combine to form the sense of plot: to talk over plans and to calculate a course of action.

'prison': dog, dogs, pack of wild dogs, chihuahua. The prison here depicts a pack of wild dogs (the long-timers and hardened criminals) into which the poor little chihuahua (firstoffender) has been cast.
'revise': nailing, words. After completing the first draft, you revise it by nailing down your words and “hammering” them into shape.
'chastise': words, glue. Words spoken to chastise us stick to us like glue in a way no other words can.

'instruction': words, stream. The personalism connoted by the word instruction, as opposed to “teaching” or “discipline,” suits the picture here of words guiding one's progress like the gentle flowing of a stream.
'imperial edict': words, seduce. The imperial edict, spoken with the force of unquestionable law, is made up of words intended to seduce the masses—be it through fear or respect—to follow obediently.
'packed': words, aerosol can. The character sees the words as sealed tightly inside an aerosol can.
'tale': words, tongue. That the words of the tongue should come to mean a tale is clear from the etymology: a tale is something “talked,” not something read from a book.
'recitation': words, eternity. Listening to the words of poets reciting their poetry is like being transported for a moment into eternity where the rules of everyday life have been suspended.
'poem': buddhist temple, words, recitation. Since silence is treasured so highly at a Buddhist temple the words spoken there must be well-chosen.
'word': say. Whereas the character for say focused on the actual talking, that for words stresses the fact that although it is I who say them, the words of a language are not my own.
'read': words, sell. In the age of advertising, most words we read are out to sell some product or point of view.
'tune': lap, words. A complete tune is composed not only of a succession of notes but also of one lap of the words that go with it.

'discuss': inflammation, words. In almost every attempt to discuss an issue, the fervor of one's convictions comes to the surface and creates an inflammation of words (if you will, the “cuss” in discuss).
'consent': words, young. The words of the young do not have legal validity unless backed up by “parental consent.”

'rebuke': words, meeting, butchers. The stern tone of a rebuke is seen here in the image of words spoken at a meeting of butchers waving their choppers at one another and “cutting one another down” as only butchers can.
'style': arrow, craft. Then let the element arrow and craft stand for the well-known style of shirts known as “Arrow shirts” because of the little arrow sewn on each one.

'test': style, speak. When a manufacturer produces a new style for the market, the first thing that is done is to run a test on consumers, asking them to speak their opinions frankly about the product.
'ii (two)': two, quiver. Think of two arrows in a quiver, standing up like the numeral ii.
'range': land, fiesta, mouth, floor. As soon as the cowboys come home, home on the range, the first thing they do is kiss the ground (the mouth on the floor), and then get on with the fiesta.

'burglar': fiesta, needle, shells. From a burglar's point of view, a fiesta is an occasion to take out the old lockpicking needle and break into the unattended safe filled with the family shells (the old form of money, as we
'plantation': trees, thanksgiving. On a fruit plantation it is the trees that one is particularly grateful for at the time of Thanksgiving.
'load': cart, thanksgiving. One loads bales on a wagon or cart in preparation for the great Hay Ride that follows the Thanksgiving dinner each year.
'overgrown': parade, flowers. The sense of the key word overgrown is of something growing luxuriously, though not necessarily in excess—in this case a whole parade of weeds (outcaste flowers).
'turn into': parade, dagger. What happens here is that the parade marching down main street turns into a dagger-throwing bout between competing bands.
'castle': dirt, turned into. In this frame, we see a mound of dirt that is being turned into a castle (the way you may have done as a child playing on the beach).
'sincerity': words, turned into. The sure sign of sincerity is that one's mere words are turned into deeds.
'intimidate': march, women. Here we see a march of women demonstrating on behalf of equal rights, something extremely intimidating to the male chauvinist population.
'destroy': march, flames, water. Picture a march of flames demonstrating against the Fire Department for their right to destroy, but being doused with water by the police riot squads.

'dwindle': mouths, march, water. A group of unquenchable mouths sets out on a march across the country, drinking water wherever they find it until the water supply has dwindled to a trickle, triggering a national disaster.
'scaffold': trees, float. Prior to the use of metal, trees were once cut down and bound together for use as scaffolding material.
'coin': gold, floats. Those special gold-colored tokens minted each year for the Mardi Gras and thrown into the crowds from people on the floats give us the kanji for coins.
'shallow': floats, water. An entourage of floats going from one town to the next must always seek a shallow place to cross the water.
'stop'. The character for stop is easiest to learn as a pictograph, though you have to take a moment to see it.
'walk': footprints, few. Footprints that follow one another a few at a time indicate walking.
'ford': water, walk. To ford a body of water means to walk across it.
'repeatedly': head walked. The image of something occurring repeatedly, over and over again, is of having one's head walked on.
'agreement': footprints, flesh. Seeing footprints on someone's flesh indicates a rather brutal way of having secured that person's agreement.
'undertake': stop, umbrella. Here we see some undertaking made to stop under a beach umbrella.

'curriculum': grove of trees, grove, cliff, stopped. Instead of the grove making its way slowly through the surface of the cliff as before, here we see it stopped, much the same as a curriculum vitae calls a halt to the

'warrior': quiver, arrows, stop. With a quiver of arrows set on one's back, the goal of the warrior depicted here is not to attack but merely to stop the attack of others: the oldest excuse in history!

'levy': shells, warrior. A certain portion of shells (money) is collected by the warrior from the local villages as he passes through to defray the costs of keeping the land safe, and this is called a levy.
'correct': one footprint. Here we see one footprint, complementing that proverb with the sound advice that if the first step is not made correctly, the whole point of the journey will be forfeited.
'evidence': words, correctness. Words that testify to the correctness of some fact are classified as evidence.
'politics': correct taskmastering, taskmastering, correctly. On the one hand, we see the pessimistic wisdom that politics has to do with taskmastering, maneuvering people with or without their will.
'determine': mending, house. Determination, in the sense of settling on a certain course of action, is likened here to mending one's house.
'lock': metal, determined. It needs to be so determined by a locksmith.
'run': mends, soil, road. Running, we are told here, mends the soil.
'transcend': running, seduces. When one is running after something, the goal that seduces one is said to transcend the seeker.

'proceed': runs, divining rod. In proceeding to a new city or a new job, something in you runs ahead with excitement, and something else holds you back, like a divining rod built into your psyche warning you to check things
'surpass': parades, running, parade. Here we see two parades in competition, each trying to surpass the other by running at high speed from one town to the next.
'just so': day, mending. In this kanji we are shown someone spending an entire day at mending one stocking, because they want the job done “just so.”
'topic': headings, just so. In many kinds of research, one can find information on a given topic only if the headings are prepared just so.
'dike': earth, just so. A dike is a successful bit of engineering only if the amount of earth piled up is measured just so for the height and pressure of the water it is meant to contain.
'build': brush, s-t-r-e-t-c-h. To construct a building, you first draw a set of plans (the writing brush) and then s-t-r-e-t-c-h your drawing out to scale in reality.

'prolong': stopping, stretch, drop, stop. This character is a kind of pictographic image of how prolonging is a clever way of stopping things by trying to stretch them out a little bit at a time (the extra drop at the

'nativity': prolongation, word. John's gospel tells us, the nativity we celebrate at Christmas had its origins at the very start of time and governs all of human history: it represents the prolongation of the eternal Word in time and space.
'cornerstone': stone, zoo, grove. This character depicts a cornerstone as a stone set at the end of a wildlife preserve (the “zoo in the grove”).

'bridegroom': woman, zoo, month, moon. What makes a man a bridegroom is obviously a woman and her dowry, here presented as a small zoo (animals were often used for this purpose in earlier societies) and a month away from it
'garment': top hat. At the top we see the top hat, and at the bottom a pictographic representation of the folds of a garment.
'tailor': garment, thanksgiving. You might think here of garment that have been specially tailored for Thanksgiving celebrations to look like traditional Pilgrim garb.
'attire': turtle, samurai, garment. The character for attire can be remembered as a picture of what we may call a “turtle-samurai” sweater.

'back': top hat, scarf, computer. An innocent looking top hat and scarf lying there in front of you, turned over, reveal a hidden computer sewn into the back of each—obviously the tools of a master spy.

'demolition': garment, eye, needle, ground. The right half of this character shows a garment woven so fine that it can pass through the eye of a needle, fittingly draped around the slithering, ethereal form of a poltergeist.
'pathetic': top hat, scarf, mouth. A drunken sod in a tattered top hat and soiled silk scarf with a giant mouth guzzling something or other gives us a pathetic character role in which W.
'distant': road, lidded crock, scarf. A distant figure on the road is such a blur it looks like a lidded crock wearing a silk scarf.

'monkey': wild dogs, lidded crock, scarf. This clever little monkey has captured an entire pack of wild dogs, locked them inside a lidded crock, and wrapped the whole thing up in a silk scarf to present to the dogcatcher.
'first time': cloak, dagger. What I leave to you is to decide on an appropriate connotation for “first time” to take advantage of them.
'linen': towels by her side. The maid, towels by her side, distributes the linen.
'sail': towel, mediocre. A sail made of a towel makes a mediocre vessel.
'hanging scroll': towel, wealthiest. A towel owned by the wealthiest tycoon in the world is made into a hanging scroll after his death and auctioned off to the highest bidder.
'cap': risk, sun, eyes, towel. Because of the risk involved (of getting the sun in one's eyes), one puts together a makeshift cap out of a dirty old towel.
'curtain': towel, graveyard. A dirty towel draped over the entrance to the old graveyard is painted to look like the curtain of death that leads to the other world.
'brocade': white towel, metal. A strip of white towel and some scraps of metal have the makings of a primitive kind of brocade.
'market': towel, top hat. Dressed in nothing but a bath towel and top hat, one sets off to the marketplace in search of a bargain or two.
'elder sister': women, market. Of all the women of the family, it is the elder sister who has the duty to go to market to do the shopping.
'lungs': market, meats. One is surprised, strolling through the market, to find among the meats hung out for sale a slab marked: lungs.
'sash': apron. The part of the apron where one finds the buckle (represented pictorially by the first 5 strokes) is on the sash.

'stagnate': sashed, water. People that have been “sashed” to something (whether their mother's apron strings or a particular job) for too long become like water that has stopped moving: they start to stagnate.
'thorn': tree, belt, sabers. Thorns grow on a bush here that has wrapped itself around a tree like a belt, cutting into the poor tree like little sabers.

'system': cows, saber, belt, cow. This kanji show a unique system for leading cows to the slaughterer's saber: one ties a belt about their waist and fixes that belt to an overhead cable, pulling the cow up into the air
'made in…': garment, systematization. A label indicating that a garment was made in U.S.A.
'revolve': car, rising clouds. As the wheels of the car revolve, they kick up small rising clouds of dust and debris behind them.
'technique': rising cloud, flowers. The secret technique of making a rising cloud of smoke turn into a bouquet of flowers is shown here.

'cloud': rising cloud, clouds, rising, rain. Clouds begin with vapors rising up in small clouds from the surface of the earth, and then gathering to make clouds that eventually dump their rain back on the earth.
'cloudy weather': sun, clouds. We refer to days when the sun is covered by the clouds as cloudy weather.

'thunder': rice field, weather. The full rumble and roar and terror of thunder is best felt not with your head tucked under your pillow safe in bed, but out in an open rice field where you can get the real

'frost': inter, weather. Think of frost as a cooperative venture, an inter-action of the malevolent forces of weather that sit around a conference table and finally decide to allow a very light amount of moisture to fall just before a
'winter': walking legs, ice. Walking legs slipping on the ice are a sure sign of winter.
'bridge': trees, angels. The bridge shown here is made of trees in their natural form, except that the trunks have been carved into the forms of angels, a sort of “Ponte degli Angeli.”

'cry': standing up, water, vase. One cries and cries until one is standing up knee-deep in water (or until one has a vase-full of water).
'badge': sunflower, vase. Try to imagine a club badge pinned to your lapel in the form of a mammoth sunflower protruding from a wee little vase.
'vie': teenagers, standing up. Two teenagers are seen here standing up to one another, vying for the attention of their peers.

'sovereign': standing up, apron. An uncommon, but not altogether unlikely picture of a reigning sovereign has him standing up in his apron, presumably at the behest of his sovereign (she who is to be obeyed), who needs help with washing

'juvenile': standing, computer. This frame shows up the image of a juvenile hacker standing on top of a computer, or rather jumping up and down on it, because it refused to come up with the right answer.
'pupil': eye, juvenile. Now all you have to do is dwell on the phrase “juvenile of one's eye” (the meaning here) until it provides you with an image.
'bell': metal, juveniles. This bell is made of cheap metal, and so badly made that when you ring it, it lets out a noise like the “bellowing” of juveniles who aren't getting their own way.
'make a deal': standing, motorcycle helmet, legs, mouth. See the peddlar standing atop his motorcycle helmet as if it were a soapbox, hawking his wares to passersby.
'legitimate wife': woman, antique. The phrase legitimate wife would have no meaning if there were not such things as “illegitimate wives,” taken because one's legal woman has turned into an antique.
'suitable': antiques, roadway. Can you imagine anything less suitable to do with one's precious antiques than to display them in the middle of a crowded roadway?
'drip': water, antiques. Picture water dripping on what you thought were precious antiques, only to find that the artificial aging painted on them is running!

'enemy': antique, taskmaster. Picture your most precious antique (it doesn't matter how old it really is, so long as it is the oldest thing you own) being knocked over by your most unlikeable taskmaster, and you have a good picture
'north'. The cold air from the north is so strong that we see two people sitting on the ground back to back, their arms interlocked so they don't blow away.
'stature': northern, part of the body. One's stature is measured according to the “northern-most” part of the body.
'compare': two spoons. With two spoons, one in each hand, you are comparing your mother's cooking with your mother-in-law's.

'descendants': comparing, sun. By comparing apes with anthropoids, we not only discover the latter have descended from those progenitors educated in the higher branches, but that the very idea of seeing everything descended from everything else, one way or another
'all': comparing, whiteness. Think of the housewives in tv commercials “comparing the whiteness” of their laundry across the fence, a typical advertisement for the popular detergent known as All.
'mix': water, descendants. Mixed marriages, this character suggests, water down the quality of one's descendants—the oldest racial nonsense in the world!
'thirst': siesta, water. As you pass by the muchacho taking the siesta, he cries out that he is thirsty and asks for something to drink.

'audience': siesta, speech. Imagine an audience with the emperor or the pope in which all those in attendance are sitting down, leaning against the wall, sleeping like our muchacho on siesta as the honorable host delivers his speech.
'brown': cloak, siesta. The color of the serape or cloak of our muchacho on siesta is a dull brown, the color this kanji indicates.
'hoarse': siesta, mouth. When the muchacho on siesta looks up at you and opens his mouth to talk, his voice is so hoarse that you cannot understand him.
'delicious': day, spoon. Something is so downright delicious that one spends the entire day with a spoon in hand gobbling it up.
'fat': flesh, delicious. This kanji tells us that if you feed the flesh with too many delicious things, it soon picks up a thick layer of fat.

'i (one)': samurai, sitting on the ground, crown. In the midst of all the samurai, we notice one in particular sitting on the ground with a crown on his head, indicating that he is “number i” in the current rankings.
'cleverness': every, taskmaster. Behind every successful taskmaster, the cleverness of a fox to outwit his charges.
'plum': every, tree. Behind every Jack Horner's piemaker, a tree full of plums.
'sea': every drop of water, water. Behind every drop of water, a sea from which all water originally came.
'beg': lying down, hook. See someone lying down in a public place with a hook in place of a hand, begging a morsel of rice or a few pence.
'drought': begging, mist. Here we see the victims begging for just a little mist for relief.
'abdomen': double back, part of the body. If you double back (fold over) most animals in the middle, the part of the body where the crease comes is the abdomen.
'duplicate': double, back, cloak. In its original and etymologically transparent sense, to duplicate something means to double it back with a fold, like the fold of a cloak.
'lack'. Since yawning shows a lack of something (psychologically, interest; physiologically, sleep), the connection is plain to see.
'blow': mouth lack. To blow is really no more than a deliberate effort to make one's mouth lack all the air that is in it.
'cook': fire, yawning. Here we see a blazing fire and an inattentive, yawning cook who let things get out of control.
'song': can-can, yawning. Why it should be eliciting nothing but yawning from the audience, I leave to you to decide.
'soft': car, yawning. If the cushions of one's car are too soft, one may begin yawning at the wheel.
'next': lack, ice. Let there be a lack of ice on the hottest day of summer, and you stand impatiently in line waiting for the distributor to call out “Next!”
'briar': second, flowers, thorn. But in the second part of the story, these briars blossomed into flowers.
'assets': shells, next shells. From then on, the next shells you accumulate become your assets.
'figure': woman's, second. This kanji depicts a woman's figure as a sort of second self.
'consult with': words, second mouth. To seek the words of a second mouth is to consult with someone about something.
'compensation': clam, muzzle. Picture a clam used as a muzzle to quiet the complaints of a fisherman's widow asking compensation for her husband lost at sea.

'cultivate': muzzling, soil. The barrel hoops used by many Japanese farmers to stretch clear plastic over row of vegetables in a garden patch in the hopes of cultivating bigger and bigger vegetables is a way of muzzling the soil.
'divide': saber, muzzle. To “divide and conquer” you use a saber and a muzzle.

'sound': standing, tongue wagging in a mouth. The kanji for sound depicts something standing in the air over a tongue wagging in a mouth, much the same as a sound does for the briefest of moments before disappearing.
'darkness': sun, sound. When “darkness covered the earth” at the beginning of time, there was neither sun nor sound.
'rhyme': sound, employee. In this kanji's picture, one becomes a kind of “sound-employee.”
'discriminating': kazoo, words. A person of discriminating intellect can tell the difference between mere kazoo-buzzing and words spoken wisely.
'mirror': metal, metal mirrors. After lakes but before glass, polished metal was used for mirrors.
'boundary': land, mirrors. Imagine the boundary of a plot of land marked with gigantic mirrors enabling the landowner to keep trespassers in sight at all times.
'deceased': top hat, hook. A top hat hanging on a hook in the front hall, right where the deceased left it the day he died, reminds us of him and his kanji.
'blind': eyes. If one's eyes perish before death, one remains blind for the rest of life.
'delusion': woman, perish. The “ideal woman” one daydreams about is no more than a delusion.
'laid waste': flowers, perish, flood. The flowers that perish in the flood are taken here as symbols of an area that has been laid waste.
'ambition': king, perishing, moon. The story of ambition talks of a king walking under the perishing (or “waning”) moon dreaming great dreams about his kingdom.

'direction': dagger, top hat. Spinning a dagger about on its hilt on the top of a top hat— waiting to see in which direction it points when it comes to rest—one leaves to fate where one is going next.
'disturb': compass, woman. Imagine a compass that is disturbed every time a woman passes by, sending the needle spinning madly round and round.
'boy': dirt, compass. The character for a boy shows us a Boy Scout cleaning the dirt out of his compass—the more dirt, the better.
'perfumed': compass, flowers. Here we see a special compass used to pick out those flowers most suited for making good perfumes.
'obese': compass, flesh, round, fat. One who eats too much soon needs a compass to find one's way around the obese mass of flesh that accumulates in the midsection.
'call on': words, compass. When making a courtesy call on a dignitary, one has to gauge one's words with great care.
'set free': taskmaster, compass. The taskmaster sets an unruly servant free, giving him no more than a quick glance at the compass and a boot from behind.
'violent': taskmaster, white, water, compass. In the white foam that covers the water we see a broken compass floating, all that remains of a shipwreck.
'undress': flesh, devil. To undress is to expose the flesh and tempt the devil in the eyes of one's onlookers.
'rumor': devil's, words. Not inappropriately, this character likens a rumor to the devil's own words.
'pointed': metal, devil's. Metal that has been pointed (as an awl, a pick, a nail, or a knife) tends to serve the devil's purposes as well as civilization's: our tools are also our weapons.
'formerly': horns, brain, tongue wagging in the mouth
'increase': soil. This kanji depicts an increase of soil, multiplying so fast that it literally buries everything in its path.
'presents': money, increases. The presents offered here are money that increases each time you give it away.
'east': sun, tree. In more fanciful terms, we see the sun piercing through a tree as it rises in the east.
'ridgepole': wood, east. If the piece of wood in the roof known as the ridgepole points east, the sunrise will be visible from the front door.
'frozen': ice, east. The whole secret to breaking the ice with the East is to peek behind those mysteriously “frozen smiles.”
'pregnancy': woman, porter. A woman who is in her pregnancy is a bit like a porter, bearing her new companion wherever she goes.
'courts': porters, stretch. Those who rule the courts, the porters of justice and order, are often found to stretch the law to suit their own purposes.
'prefecture': eye of a needle, little, eye, fishhook. Above, the eye of a needle, and below the primitive for little.
'horse chestnut': a tree, cliff, ten thousand
'ground': soil, scorpion. Soil and a scorpion (an “earth animal”).
'pond': water, scorpion, drop by drop. But if you picture rather a scorpion letting its venom out drop by drop until it has made a whole pond of the stuff, the image is more likely to remain fixed.
'wind': windy, drops of, insects, gnats. Hint: think of the last two primitives as representing a swarm of gnats, those tiny drops of pesky insects.
'reformation': snake, taskmaster, reformer, snakes. Pluralizing the snake and focusing on a single taskmaster may help recommend the image of Ireland's most famous reformer, St.
'tortoise': turtle, bound up, suns. This is not a turtle but a tortoise, however you wish to picture the difference.
'dragon': vase, eel, sign of the dragon
'consummate': horns, sow, road. The horns atop the sow suggest a boar at work in the background.
'beauty': large sheep. Try to think of what the Chinese were on to when they associated the idea of beauty with a large sheep.
'accomplished': road, soil, a sheep. On the road we find soil over a sheep.
'envious': sheep, water, yawn lack, next. Note, too, that the water comes under the sheep, rather than on its own to the left.
'don': wool, eyes. I cannot resist doing this one for you, since it clearly describes donning (putting on) one's clothes as “pulling the wool over one's eyes.”
'stirred up': st bernard dog, turkey, rice field, brains
'rob': burglary, st bernard dog, turkey, glue. Whereas burglary ( frame 357) implies clandestine appropriation of another's property, robbery refers to taking by force.
'assurance': rock, house, turkey, turkey house. On the left you see the rock, which is familiar enough.
'noon': cow. That gives the primary meaning of the Chinese zodiacal sign of the horse, which corresponds to the hour of noon.
'delight': flying horses, yawning. As dusk sets in, the flying horses all start yawning and pair off for the night: a perfectly delightful portrait of delight.
'feathers'. From the pictograph of two bird-wings, we get feathers.
'-times': a mouth, pent in. The suffix “-times” refers to a number of repetitions.
'hemp': cave, grove. If it helps, this is the hemp marijuana comes from.
a simple clear picture of 'shish kebab' (pictograph)
'grace': cause, heart. Take grace in its sense of a favor freely bestowed, not in its meaning of charming manners or fluid movement.

'recess': tongue, nose, heart, breath. The sense of breath from the last frame should not be used in your story, since it might lead us later to put only the nose over the heart and leave the tongue off to
'melancholy': head, crown, heart, walking legs. First, the doubling-up of the last stroke of head with the top of the crown serves to make the whole more aesthetically beautiful.

'lament': eminence, the state of mind. To keep this character distinct from others of similar connotation, one need only think of the Prophet Jeremiah whose poetry gave an eminence to the state of mind we call lamentation.

'enlightenment': five holes, state of mind. I know of an Indian religious sect which teaches that enlightenment is to be had by covering the eyes with one's index fingers, the ears with the thumbs, and the mouth with the little
'remorse': state of mind, emotion. Hint: the etymology of “remorse” indicates a memory that returns again and again to “bite at” one's conscience and disturb one's peace of mind.

'invariably': heart, the heart. If one takes it as a pictograph “dividing” the heart in half, then one has one of those invariably true bits of human anatomy: the fact that each heart is divided into two halves.
'hand'. Any way you count them, there are either too many or too few fingers to see a good pictograph of a hand in this character.
'sacrifice': cow, righteousness. Do not use the image of an animal sacrifice here, as that will have it own character later on.
'nose': two hands, nostrils, brain. Imagine taking your two hands and reaching up into someone's nostrils.
'genius': finger. Whatever one is particularly adept at—one's special “genius”—one can do very easily, “with one finger” as the phrase goes.
'suppose': genie in the bottle, a child
'length': arms, large. The length whose measure this kanji depicts extends from the tip of one hand to the tip of the other with arms at full length.
'history': a mouth, tucked under the arm
'officer': one, mouth, tucked under the arm
'grow late': ceiling, sun, tucked under the arm. The implication behind the meaning of grow late is that things are changing in the same way that the day turns into night.

review: câu chuyện không nêu thành phần/hình ảnh

scene: 'pair': crotch. The crotch reduplicated gives us a pair.
'mulberry': crotches, tree. Hint: think of a group of children playing an original version of “Here We Go 'Round the Mulberry Bush.”
'bough': tree, branch, twig. Take a moment to focus on the differences between a bough, a branch, and a twig ( frame 298).
'doth': climax, taskmaster. It is made up of climax and taskmaster.
'mutually': walls. When you draw this character think of linking two walls together, one right side up and the other upside down.
'current': water, infant, flood. Be sure to distinguish the two waterprimitives from one another in making your story.
'exit': earth. The kanji for exit pictures a series of mountain peaks coming out of the earth.
'mountain'. Note the clearer outline of a triangular mountain here.
'enter'. This character is meant to be a picture of someone walking leftwards, putting one leg forward in order to enter someplace.
'valley': go in, umbrella, a mouth, mouth
'contain': house, valley. This character depicts a house so large that it can contain an entire valley.
'abundant': cloak, valley. This character shows the typical cloak of valley folk, which, unlike the tailor-made, high-fashion overcoats of city folk, is loose-fitting and free-form.
'party': human legs, outhouse. Think of this key word as referring to a political party, not a gala affair.
'pelt': branch. The simplest way to remember this character is to see it as built up from that for branch.
'ear': eye. The pictograph for the ear looks much like that for eye, but note how the stroke order gives it a different look.
'shame': ear, heart. It is most rare to have the heart at the right, rather than at the bottom.
'pocket': state of mind, needle, eyes, garment
'voiced': water, eye, bound up, insect. For example, in English a “j” is voiced while a “sh” is unvoiced.
'lose': defeat, husband. It pictures a husband with something falling from his side as he is walking along, something he loses.
'retainer'. The “pop-eye” image belongs to an Emperor's retainer standing in awe before his ruler.
'gigantic': slave, retainer. Be sure not to confuse it with the slave (retainer) we just learned.

review: câu chuyện không nêu thành phần/hình ảnh

scene: 'add': muscles, mouth, muscle. This is the only case in which the primitive for muscle appears on the left; note should be taken of the fact in composing one's story.
'armpit': part of the body, muscles, triceps
'equilibrium': boulevard, bound up, brains, st bernard dog
'second': wheat, few. The reference here is to a second of time.
'core': a drop, pent in, rice, st bernard dog
'lacquer': water, tree, umbrella, grains of rice
'request': drop, arrowhead, needle, grains of rice. Let the drop in the upper right-hand corner of this character close the right angle off to make an arrowhead.
'bamboo': nail. Bamboo grows upwards, like a straight nail, and at each stage of its growth (which legend associates with the arrival of the new moon) there is a jointed rootstock (the first stroke).
'muscle': bamboo, part of the body, power
'sponsor': hermit, turkey, mountain. In order to make room for the turkey, it was raised and condensed.

'fell': person, fiesta. Hint: recall the German legend of the English missionary, Saint Boniface, who felled the sacred oak tree dedicated to Thor at Geismar (in lower Hessia), occasioning a great fiesta for the Christians in the neighborhood to mark

'furrow': top hat's, rice field's, long time. Think of the three kinds of furrows shown here in this character—a top hat's rim, a rice field's ridges, and the wrinkles that show you've been around a long time.
'meat': inside, insides, flesh, part of the body
'by means of': person, plow, drop of. Picture a person dragging a plow behind, and the drop of sweat which falls from his brow as he does his work.
'Shinto shrine': spine, house. Here a Shinto shrine is composed of house and spine.
'year': horse, sunglasses. Think of it as a horse wearing sunglasses with one of the lenses popped out.
'yell': mouth, four st bernard dogs bound up, four, st bernard. Together they should supply a clear enough portrait of a yell, provided you are careful to see all four of them.
'interchange': fingers, four st bernard dogs bound up
'shaku': shaku hachi, flag. Since the shaku is about one foot in length, this makes about 20 inches.
'show': two, little. Something placed atop the altar is put on show for all to see.
'company': altar, soil. The company referred to here is that of the modern business world.

'wherefore': rice field, flower, seedling. It does this graphically by depicting a seed in a rice field sending up a single sprout, which is the whole why and wherefore of the seed's falling in the earth and dying.
'speaketh': tongue wagging in the mouth, walking stick. It is written by a tongue wagging in the mouth with a walking stick rammed through it and coming out at both ends.

'fruit': tree, brains, rice field. The final stage of the seed is reached when the plant has reached its full growth (the tree) and comes to fruition, producing fruit full of new seeds that can return to the earth and
'fold': fingers. Hint: make an image out of the Japanese art of “origami” (paper-folding).
'departed': fold, road. The connotation is of a “dearly departed” who has passed away.
'snow': rain, broom. Rain that undergoes a change so that it can be swept aside with a broom is snow.
'demand': rain, comb. The sense of demand is best captured by thinking of the economic principle of “supply and demand.”
a simple clear picture of 'Big Dipper' (pictograph)

'map': pent in, big dipper. It referred to the nighttime travel of runaway slaves (those pent in) who had no maps other than the stars to guide them, among them the bright and predominant Big Dipper, the “Drinking Gourd.”
'pity': state of mind, once upon a time
'set aside': fingers, once upon a time
'judgment': half, saber. You might recall the famous judgment of King Solomon, who offered to slice a baby in two with a saber to give half to each of the mothers who claimed it as her own.
'one-sided'. When that picture's right side is isolated, it becomes the kanji for one-sided, in the sense of only one part of a whole.
'negative': ceiling, person, a drop of, but
'dart': heavens, drop. When shot high into the heavens, the dart gets so small it looks like a mere drop.
'halberd'. The halberd's battle-ax head and long shaft are depicted here.
'bow': bowstring. Later we will learn how to make the bowstring that goes with it ( frame 1386).
'strong': vast, insect, elbow. Note how the elbow of vast is shrunken and elevated to make room for the insect beneath.
'boast': words, st bernard dog, ceiling, snare
'somebody': nose, oneself. Its composition is based on the nose (which, you will recall, is also the kanji for oneself).

'old man': venerable old man, somebody, nose, soil. But there is another, simpler way to remember it all: the soil drawn first indicates that one has come close to the age when “dust to dust” begins to take on a
'bureaucrat': maestro's, drop, house. By replacing the maestro's baton (the drop) with the roof of a house, we have his equivalent in the institutional world of big government: the bureaucrat.

'father': taskmaster, drops. The kindness and hard work of the ideal father is seen in this abbreviation of the taskmaster that leaves off his rod or whip (the first stroke) and replaces it with the sweat of the father's brow
'merit': mingle, power, achievement. Note the distinct connotations that separate merit from achievement ( frame 863).
'leg': mouth, mending. Note that the last stroke of mouth and the first of mending overlap.
'story': pinnacle, all. The story of this character refers to floors in a building.

'hill': axes. Since this supposedly pictographic representation of a hill looks like anything but, picture a row of axes driven into the ground up to their heads, and see if that doesn't present a more memorable image of hill—at least
'thread': elbows, little. Remember when your granny used to ask you to bend your arms at the elbows and hold them out so that she could use them like a rack to hold a skein of string or yarn (here
'thong': thread, puppet. Although we usually think of a thong as coming at the end of a piece of string, this character's meaning allows for it to come at the beginning as well.

'promise': thread, ladle. Consider for a moment the etymology of the word “promise” in order to notice its roots in the activity of putting one thing (e.g., one's word of honor) in place of another (e.g., the fulfillment of a
'netting': thread, glass canopy, animal horns, perish
'faint': two cocoons, mountain, the mountain. Observe how the two vertical strokes of the mountain are extended upwards to serve as a kind of enclosure.
'shins': part of the body, instead, legs. It can also indicate the part of the legs from the shins down, which explains the choice of the key word.
'wholesale': a horse, footprint, stamp. The left primitive is a union of a horse and footprint.
'clothing': flesh, stamp, crotch. Note how the stamp is stretched out here.
'fate': fit, stamp. The bottom portion of fit is nudged to the left in order to make room for the stamp.
'trade': receipt, dagger, shells, make a deal

'entertain': staples, same, tool. On both sides you see the staples separating one number's slot from the next, and between them the character for the same—indicating that it has been fixed to repeat the same number.
'waver': wild dogs, animal horns, whiskey bottle
'beans'. This kanji depicts a pot of beans, although it looks more like a table on which the pot is resting.
'bountiful': bend, table. Think of a bountiful harvest, and you will not be far from the meaning of this character.
'blood': drop, dish, dagger, blade. The drop in the dish is blood.
'boom': turn into, dish. Here boom refers to something that is popular and prospering.

'eat': halo, umbrella, drop, silver. But you might also try breaking the halo down into drop and silver, which would give you “silverware,” an additional primitive meaning that could come in useful later on.
'bosom': part of the body, bound up, villain
'spicy': stand, needles. This character pictures food whose taste is so hot and spicy that it makes the hairs on your body stand up as straight as needles.
'forces': rice seedlings, ground, fat man, muscle
'heat': rice seedlings, ground, fat man, oven fire
'pledge': grow up, dagger, st bernard dog, vow
'enroll': bamboo, christmas tree, once upon a time
'droop': a drop of, silage, walking stick, floor
'now': mouth, meeting. If you need any help at all with this character, you may picture it as two hands of a clock pointing to what time it is now.
'shade': sunshine, pinnacle, clock, rising cloud. Just as the sunshine ( frame 1300) represents the masculine principle in nature (Yang), the shade stands for the feminine principle (Yin).
'concurrently': the animal horns, rake. Below that, we see one rake with two handles.
'west': four, one, human legs, mouth. But since we want only one of the four directions, the west adds the one at the top and sucks the human legs a bit out of their mouth in the process.
'transition': west, st bernard dog, snake, road
'south': belt, happiness. Note how the belt runs through the middle of happiness.
'interval': gates, sun, day. This interval applies to time and space alike, but the latter is better for creating an image.
'godown': gate, meeting of gates, mouth, storehouse. The single gate is used here not in order to represent one gate, but many of them, indeed a meeting of gates.
'un-'. From there to “un-” is but a short step.
'dry'. Spin it around quickly in your mind's eye to give it the connotation of to dry.
'bundle': sun, tree, east, mouth. In the same way that we saw the sun in the tree in the kanji for east, here we see a square container in the shape of a mouth.
'imperial order': imperial edict, bundle, muscle. Then it will not be hard to put together bundle and muscle to form a story about an imperial order.

'rapidly': quick, swift, darts, sickness. Picture a succession of poison darts (the sort that inflict sickness) flying out rapid-fire from a blowgun, so that “rapid-fire” can conjure up the proper image.
'ward': box, sheaves. The ward referred to here is a subdivision of a large city.
'carve': circumference, shape, engraving. The two primitives here, circumference and shape, belong naturally to the special connotations that differentiate carving from engraving .
'ought': shape, head. This is the only time that shape is placed to the left of its relative element, the head.
'swell': part of the body, drum, shape, expand
'sentence': top hat. Under the familiar top hat we see a crisscross pattern or design, like that found on woodwork or garments.
'dose': adjust, saber. Think of this as a dose of medicine.
'center': st bernard. Bernard with its head and paws keeping their stick-like form, but with the middle or center of its body filled out in a box-like shape.
'period': bushel basket, month. As the month indicates, this has to do with periods of time.

'tremendously': bushel basket, equal, animal legs, human legs. Note how the first stroke of equal doubles up with the sixth stroke of the bushel basket, and how the animal legs of the bushel basket are dropped to make room for
'dispatch': maestro's, purse, road, chased. The road represents his being dispatched on his way as an obvious misfit.
'dance': reclining, tub, sunglasses. The top two strokes show someone reclining, and the next six are a pictograph of an oaken tub ribbed with metal strips, like the kind once used for bathing.
'nothingness': tub, oven fire. Make use of the oaken tub from the previous frame, and add to that the oven fire at the bottom.
'help': shelf, power, add. The reason why the shelf appears on the left here is that the right side is the normal position for power, the stronger primitive.
'profession': in a row upside down, not yet
'slap': fingers, upside down in a row, husbands
'me': person, husbands, in a row upside down. As a rule, it is a word that boys and men use to refer to themselves.
'submit': person, strung together. Submit here is a transitive verb, meaning to offer or present.
'angle': bound up, glass canopy, walking stick, two
'again': jewel, belt. Note how the belt is drawn right after the first stroke of jewel.
'people': drop, family name, mouth. In place of the drop at the start of the character for family name, we have a mouth, which makes you think of the “vox populi.”
'grade': staples, staple gun, missile. Hence, we call it a staple gun.
'liner': boat, dove. Don't count on size alone to distinguish the boat from the liner.

'cocoon': insect, flowers, thread, hood. The silkworm (insect) eats the leaves of the mulberry bush (the flowers), digests them and transforms them into thread with which it spins about itself, in mystic wisdom, its own coffin (the hood).
'benefit': dish, animal horns, animal legs. What we have poised over the dish here is a pair of animal horns that are attached to a pair of animal legs by a single horizontal stroke.
'spare time': day, staples, mouth, box. Next to it we see staples being held in mouth (one stroke is doubled up), indicating working in one's hobby or handicrafts at home on one's spare time.
'spread': arrowhead, rice field, brains, compass. At the top we have the arrowhead whose vertical line joins it to the rice field (or brains) below it.
'vapor': spirit, sheaves, water. Simply replace sheaves with drops of water on the left in order to get vapor.
'fly': large hooks, drops, hook, measuring box. The two large hooks have little propellers (the two drops on each hook) attached to them for flying.
'sink': crown, leg, water. Rather than the biblical image of tying a millstone about the victim's neck, here we see a crown tied about one leg before the unfortunate party is tossed into the water.

'decline': top hat, scarf, walking stick, mouth. It shows a fellow in a top hat and scarf, trying hard to look happy by putting a walking stick in his mouth sideways to twist his face into a grotesque but semipermanent
'inmost': top hat, scarf, walking stick, mouth. Between the top hat and the scarf you will see the character for in which is truncated at the bottom so as not to interfere with the scarf.

'mask': eyes, hundred, eye. Imagine a mask over your head with eyes not only peeping out of the normal place, but all over the head, a hundred in all (the element for eye displacing the fifth stroke of that for
'leather': flowers, car. Think of the seats having been taken out so that they can be reupholstered with this decorated leather.
'voice': samurai, flag. The combination beneath, which looks like a flag with a line running through it, is not.
'give': mouth, tool. The mouth and tool are already familiar.
'steam': flower, floor, oven fire, complete. The flower at the top and the floor with the oven fire beneath are familiar.

'tusk': box, halberd. If you play with this primitive's form with pencil and paper, you will see that it begins with a box-like shape, and ends with the final two strokes of the halberd, a convenient combination for the tusk
'fur': hand. If you reverse your hand and put its palm down, you will have the side on which fur grows.
'long': hair, hairpin. In line with the story of the preceding frame, the hair that needs the hairpin is long.
'hair of the head': hair, shape, friend
'brain': part of the body, owl, villain, brains
'chain': metal, little, shells, owl. We have saved this character until now in order to draw attention to the visual difference between the owl and little.
'game hunting': pack of wild dogs, owl, wind, cornstalk
'island': bird's tail, mountain. The bird's tail is tucked under here, because it has come to stop on a mountain to rest from its journey across the waters.

'accidentally': person, insect, brain, belt. As for the right side, we may combine the insect with a brain (observe the writing) and a belt to create the Talking Cricket who served as Pinocchio's conscience.
'Mount': mountain goat, glass canopy. Here we see a a mountain goat “mounted” under a glass canopy.
'tin can': horse, mountain. Though the meaning has no reference to animals, the parts do: horse with a mountain underneath.
'groundbreaking': skunk, silver, soil. The groundbreaking referred to here is not for the erection of new buildings but for the opening of farmlands.
'elephant': rabbit's, sow. A rabbit's head with the body of a sow represents an elephant.
'horse': mane, tail feathers. The only odd thing is the tail feathers at the end, but that should present a good image to remember the character by.

'pony': team of horses, phrase, phrases. In American slang, a pony is an underground translation of a classical text, which students who cannot manage the difficult phrases of the original language consult and pass on from one generation to the

'tiger': magic wand, diced, human legs, zoo. It seems that each of them knew how to make one part of the beast, so they pooled their talents and brought all the pieces (diced into pieces) together, at which point the
'deer': caves, comparing, locked, lock. But more important than the enigmas of the troglodytic mind is the way in which caves, a double-lock, and comparing gives us the kanji for deer.
'lovely': deer, mediocre, ceiling. The painting of a deer itself with its form and color is enough to fill the bill for an image of something lovely.
'ability': bear. For instance, you might imagine that the test of ability envisioned here is removing the bear from the oven fire.
'with child': woman, sign of the dragon, pregnant
'ghost': drop of, brains, human legs, elbow
